headline: Bus fares up 17 paisa/km as fuel price hike triggers transport cost surge across Bangladesh
summary: Following a Tk 20 per litre increase in fuel prices, bus fares have officially risen, while launch and truck operators are already charging higher rates, adding financial strain on commuters and businesses.
details: Bus fares across Bangladesh have officially increased by 17 paisa per kilometre following a Tk 20 per litre hike in diesel, octane, petrol, and kerosene prices. Long-distance bus fares now stand at Tk 2.40/km, up from Tk 2.23, while metropolitan fares rose from Tk 2.53 to Tk 2.70/km.

Even before government approval, launch and freight operators have begun raising fares. Passengers at Sadarghat reported launch operators charging higher rates, with a deck ticket to Bhola increasing from Tk 300-350 to Tk 400.

On the Dhaka-Barishal route, deck fares have jumped from Tk 300 to Tk 350, single cabins from Tk 1,000 to Tk 1,200, and double cabins from Tk 2,000 to Tk 2,400. Similar increases are reported on Chandpur and Aricha routes.

Launch owners stated they cannot operate at a loss after the fuel price increase and have submitted a proposal for new fares. Truck and lorry fares are also expected to be fixed within this week, with owners citing additional operational costs.

The fuel price hike has significantly impacted freight transport, particularly at Benapole land port. Truck owners have increased fares by Tk 5,000 to Tk 6,000 per trip for imported and export goods, creating difficulties for traders.
Road Transport and Bridges Minister Shaikh Rabiul Alam warned truck owners against indiscriminate fare increases. He assured that launch fares would be reviewed after discussions with owners.

headline: Dhaka University student returns home due to lack of funds after 5 months, education uncertain
summary: Alamin Hossain, a first-year DU student, had to leave his studies and return to his village in Kushtia as his family cannot afford the monthly expenses of BDT 5,000-6,000. His future at the university is now uncertain.
details: Alamin Hossain, a 20-year-old first-year student at Dhaka University's Institute of Social Welfare and Research, has been forced to return to his village home in Kushtia. Despite being admitted to the prestigious university with borrowed money, his studies are now uncertain due to extreme financial hardship.

Alamin's family lives in Rajapur village, Kumarkhali Upazila, Kushtia. His father, Alef Ali, works as a van driver, earning only BDT 400-500 daily. He supports a large family including Alamin, his second wife, an elderly mother, and three other school-going children.

Alamin is a brilliant student, achieving GPA-5 in both SSC (2023) and HSC (2025) from the Commerce and Humanities groups respectively. He prepared for university admission tests for free at a coaching center after passing a scholarship exam, securing 20th position in Jahangirnagar University's 'C' unit and 526th in Dhaka University's 'B' unit.

He managed to get admitted to Dhaka University with the help of local community support and loans. However, after just two months of staying in a hall, the monthly expenses of BDT 5,000-6,000 for living and studying became unsustainable. He returned home last Thursday, while his friends are now preparing for semester finals.

Alamin's father, Alef Ali, expressed his distress, stating that his meager income is barely enough to run the household. He described his son's education expenses as a "tyranny" he cannot bear, leading to Alamin's return from Dhaka.

Alamin's stepmother, Roksana Begum, also confirmed his academic excellence and the family's desire for him to continue his studies. However, she lamented their inability to provide the necessary financial support.

Alamin's life story is marked by tragedy; his mother, Kajoli Khatun, died by suicide in 2023 due to overwhelming debt and poverty. After this immense loss, his education nearly stopped, but he persevered with the support of villagers and relatives.

Neighbors describe Alamin as a humble and talented young man. They recall his mother's tragic death and emphasize the significance of his admission to Dhaka University, urging everyone to stand by him to ensure his education continues.

Alamin is emotionally distraught, revealing he has an exam next Sunday and has managed to collect some money to travel to Dhaka for it. However, he remains uncertain and worried about his future beyond this immediate hurdle.
